rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday word for a skin blister.

example.english: I got a blister on my toe after hiking.
example.traditional: 我行完山，腳趾磨到起咗個水泡。
example.jyutping: ngo5 haang4 jyun4 saan1 goek3 zi2 mo4 dou3 hei2 zo2 go3 seoi2 paau3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when a person or body part develops blisters.

example.english: I walked mountain trails all day, and my feet began to blister.
example.traditional: 我行咗成日山路，對腳開始起水泡喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 haang4 zo2 seng4 jat6 saan1 lou6 deoi3 goek3 hoi1 ci2 hei2 seoi2 pok1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for paint, plaster, or another surface that bubbles or forms blisters rather than for skin.

example.english: The paint started to blister after it dried.
example.traditional: 油漆乾咗之後，牆身開始起泡。
example.jyutping: jau4 cat1 gon1 zo2 zi1 hau6 coeng4 san1 hoi1 ci2 hei2 pok1

rows.note: Use this causative construction when something makes A develop blisters.

example.english: Those shoes made my feet blister.
example.traditional: 對流鞋令我對腳起水泡。
example.jyutping: deoi3 lau4 haai4 ling6 ngo5 deoi3 goek3 hei2 seoi2 paau1

rows.note: Use this specifically for blister-pack packaging with moulded plastic cavities.

example.english: These earphones come in blister packaging, and you have to cut open the plastic shell to get them out.
example.traditional: 呢盒耳機用吸塑包裝，拆嗰陣要剪開個膠殼。
example.jyutping: ni1 hap6 ji5 gei1 jung6 kap1 sou3 baau1 zong1 caak3 go2 zan6 jiu3 zin2 hoi1 go3 gaau1 hok3
